title: Falling Sand action simulator in space
author: jma-dev
selftext:
I've been prototyping this idea for many years, but never managed to bring it to completion until now. The scope and effort to make the simulation part work well was never on the table because of the necessary time investment.

It's a fully destructible pixel level physics simulated game in space, where the player construct and upgrade their own battle machine throughout a vast map in the campaign giving many, many hours of entertainment.

During the prototyping phase, I was testing various engines and frameworks and it stood between these 4: Unity with ECS, Raylib, MonoGame and FNA. At the end, MonoGame was the winner. It could handle the largest amount of moving sprites interacting with each other without slowing down. This was a surprise, given it's made in C# and not C++ like RayLib. It was very convenient for me as I have vast experience with C#.

MonoGame is extremely efficient at sending data from cpu to gpu using an extremely optimized batching system. The problem; It's inherently single threaded. Because of the simulation scope I wanted to achieve, it wouldn't work. This part required a LOT of hand holding and pointing the AI to research papers, special programming techniques and other esoteric ways of doing optimization. At the end, I'm happy with the result.

I've been juggling between Google, OpenAI, Claude and DeepSeek as AI providers. To make this work well, I've created my own Agent Orchestration system. This system help move seamless between providers and models. The system itself determines what model need to be used on a specific task. This improves the token usage tremendously. I can spawn projects to multiple computers and they can all reference each other. There are many open source alternatives, but I believe in tuning the harness to my own preferences.

The Steam Store Page is out: [https://store.steampowered.com/app/5272000/Gravitonia/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/5272000/Gravitonia/)

The game will be released on December 17th. Take a look and wishlist the game if interested.
